findings.fix: After the delegation above, replace the `locSubring` proofs by applications of the general lemmas (e.g. `locSubring_le_iff := locBaseSubring_le_iff …`, `divBy_mem_locSubring := divBy_mem_locBaseSubring …`). For that to be one line, state `locBaseSubring_le_iff`'s first conjunct in the same `∀ a ∈ B, algebraMap A S a ∈ C` form the existing `locSubring_le_iff` uses, instead of the set-image inclusion at line 112.
findings.issue: Each new lemma repeats the proof script of its existing counterpart instead of reusing it: `divBy_mem_locBaseSubring` (l.103-104) is character-identical to `divBy_mem_locSubring` (l.175-176), `algebraMap_mem_locBaseSubring` (l.96-97) reproves `algebraMap_ringOfDefinition_subset_locSubring`/`algebraMap_mem_locSubring` (l.169, 183), `locBaseSubring_le_iff` (l.113-116) reproves `locSubring_le_iff` (l.194-199), and `locBaseSubring_def` reproves `locSubring_def`. Two copies of the same reasoning now have to be kept in step.

summary: The bridge `locSubring_eq_locBaseSubring` is a bare `rfl` between two independently written definition bodies rather than a definitional delegation, and every new `locBaseSubring` interface lemma re-proves verbatim the proof already present for its `locSubring` counterpart. Making `locSubring` unfold to `locBaseSubring` makes the bridge structurally true and lets each specialised lemma be a one-line application.
